title: Polish Rye Sour Cream Breakfast Soup
summary: Transforming traditional Polish comfort food into an invigorating morning meal, this unique breakfast soup revamps classic sour rye flavors. Featuring a foundation of fermented rye sourdough starter, the creamy broth is gently simmered with smoked marjoram, diced root vegetables, and fragrant garlic cloves. To make it morning-friendly, soft poached eggs and delicate potato-chive dumplings are nestled directly into the steaming bowl just before serving. A touch of heavy sour cream and fresh dill creates a silky texture that coats the spoon with soothing warmth. Diced pan-fried caraway bacon provides a savory crunch that balances the characteristic tartness of the soup. Designed to provide long-lasting energy for the day ahead, this hearty dish offers an authentic taste of Eastern European hospitality in a vibrant breakfast format. Serve hot with thick slices of toasted sourdough bread spread with cultured butter to complete a comforting start to your morning routine that will leave everyone thoroughly satisfied.

steps.step: Pour vegetable broth into a heavy soup pot and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Peel carrot parsley root and celeriac bulb then dice into small uniform cubes.
Add diced root vegetables dried bay leaves and allspice berries to simmering broth.
Mince garlic cloves finely and add to broth along with dried marjoram leaves.
Simmer broth uncovered for fifteen minutes until root vegetables are soft.
Dice smoked bacon into quarter inch cubes using a sharp utility knife.
Heat butter in a separate frying pan over medium heat for one minute.
Add diced bacon and caraway seeds to pan and cook until crisp golden brown.
Transfer cooked bacon to paper towels using slotted spoon leaving rendered fat.
Shake fermented rye starter jar well to suspend settled flour prior to pouring.
Whisk fermented rye starter gradually into simmering vegetable broth pot.
Simmer soup continuously for five minutes until liquid thickens slightly.
Whisk sour cream and horseradish paste together in a small ceramic bowl.
Ladle hot soup slowly into sour cream bowl to temper cream before adding.
Combine cold mashed potatoes all purpose flour and chopped chives in bowl.
Season potato dumpling dough mixture with salt black pepper and paprika.
Knead potato dough briefly with clean hands until smooth ball dough forms.
Pinch off small tablespoon sized pieces of dough and roll into smooth balls.
Press thumb gently into center of each dumpling ball to create small dimple.
Bring a separate pot of salted water to gentle boil for cooking dumplings.
Drop potato dumplings into boiling water carefully using slotted spoon.
Cook dumplings for three minutes after they float to surface of boiling water.
Remove cooked dumplings with slotted spoon and transfer to clean warm plate.
Drizzle dumplings lightly with bacon fat from skillet to prevent sticking.
Keep cooked dumplings covered loosely with foil in warm area of kitchen.
Prepare poaching bath by filling wide shallow skillet with two inches water.
Add white vinegar to poaching water and bring to gentle barely bubbling simmer.
Crack fresh eggs into individual small ramekins for easy poaching drop.
Pour tempered sour cream mixture back into soup pot while stirring constantly.
Season soup with salt and freshly ground black pepper according to taste preference.
Keep soup on lowest heat setting so cream does not curdle or separate.
Slide cracked eggs gently into simmering poached water bath one at a time.
Poach eggs for exactly three minutes until whites set and yolks remain runny.
Remove poached eggs carefully with slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.
Divide cooked potato dumplings evenly among four wide prewarmed soup bowls.
Ladle hot rye sour cream soup over dumplings in bowls leaving room for egg.
Place one poached egg gently into center of each soup bowl onto dumplings.
Garnish soup bowls generously with crisp caraway bacon and chopped fresh dill.
Toast sourdough bread slices until golden brown and spread with cultured butter.
Serve steaming breakfast soup immediately accompanied by warm sourdough toast.
Instruct diners to break poached egg yolk into soup broth before eating.
Provide extra fresh dill and horseradish at table for customized seasoning.
